items.a: Yes! ZChess is completely free. Create an account and start playing immediately with access to all core features.

items.q: How does the rating system work?
items.a: ZChess uses an Elo-based rating system. Your rating changes based on the result of your games and the rating of your opponent. Win against stronger players to gain more points.
Absolutely! ZChess is fully responsive and works on all devices. You can also install it as a PWA app from your browser for the best mobile experience.

items.q: How does the XP and leveling system work?
items.a: You earn XP by playing games, winning matches, completing daily quests, and unlocking achievements. Each level requires progressively more XP, and reaching new levels unlocks cosmetic rewards like profile frames and titles.

items.q: How does the AI difficulty work?
items.a: We have 7 difficulty levels. Beginner plays random moves. Higher levels use deeper search algorithms. Grandmaster and Impossible levels play near-perfectly and are a serious challenge even for experienced players.

items.q: How do I create a private game?
items.a: Go to Play > Private Room > Create Room. You'll receive a room code that you can share with your friend so they can join.

items.q: How do I undo a move?
items.a: Undo is only available in games against the AI. During online multiplayer matches, undo is not available to keep gameplay fair.

items.q: What happens if I disconnect mid-game?
items.a: In online multiplayer, you have 30 seconds to reconnect before the game is forfeited. Games against AI are saved automatically and you can resume them.

sections.title: The Objective
sections.content: The goal of chess is to checkmate your opponent's king - put it in a position where it is under attack and cannot escape.

sections.title: The Pieces
sections.content: Each player starts with 16 pieces: 1 King, 1 Queen, 2 Rooks, 2 Bishops, 2 Knights, and 8 Pawns. White always moves first.

sections.title: How Pieces Move
sections.content: King: one square in any direction. Queen: any number of squares in any direction. Rook: any number of squares horizontally or vertically. Bishop: any number of squares diagonally. Knight: L-shape (2+1 squares), can jump over pieces. Pawn: one square forward (two from starting position), captures diagonally.

sections.title: Special Moves
sections.content: Castling: Move king two squares toward a rook; the rook jumps to the other side. En passant: A pawn that just moved two squares can be captured as if it only moved one. Promotion: A pawn reaching the opposite end promotes to Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight.

sections.title: Check, Checkmate & Draw
sections.content: Check: The king is under attack and must move out. Checkmate: The king cannot escape check - the game ends. Draw: Stalemate (no legal moves, not in check), insufficient material, 50-move rule, or threefold repetition.
